newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss sight deposits don't fully show SNB policy.
newsitem.headline: Swiss sight deposits don't fully show SNB policy.

text.p: The Swiss National Bank's (SNB) latest statement showing sight deposits fell to 3,018.3 million Swiss francs in late August does not fully reflect the bank's injections of generous liquidity to the money market, a SNB spokesman said.
"This does not fully reflect the high levels we have added to the money market," the spokesman told Reuters. "This does not reflect how generous we have been."
He pointed out that there was no tightness in the money market as shown by developments in short-term interest rates.

The SNB has stated it has provided generous liquidity to the money market in what analysts have called a signal that the strictly monetarist central bank is willing to steer a slightly easier monetary course for the time being.
The bank has made clear it will keep a close eye on the Swiss franc, which has been firm of late against the dollar and mark at a time the export-dependent Swiss economy is struggling.
The SNB injects liquidity primarily through currency swaps, but also conducts open market operations via money market claims or injections of federal funds it holds on account.
Dealers said the bank injected overnight funds actively today at around 1-3/4 percent.
SNB President Hans Meyer told the Swiss daily Tages Anzeiger that the bank was concerned about Swiss franc strength in the face of a weak domestic economy.
But the SNB was also aware that it did not have the ability to force a completely different development, he added.
"Bold intervention would be coupled with big risks. However, we are trying to smooth out the exchange rate swings," he was quoted as saying in Monday's edition.
